title: The Star Wars Holiday Special of 1978
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss The Star Wars Holiday Special (1978), the CBS variety-style TV special centered on Chewbacca's Wookiee family on Kazook celebrating Life Day while Han Solo tries to get Chewie home. They cover its origins with George Lucas and the Wookiee Bible, the variety-show concept, the writers and production (David Acomba's exit, Steve Binder finishing it), the cast (Harrison Ford, Mark Hamill, Carrie Fisher, Peter Mayhew, Harvey Korman, Bea Arthur, Art Carney, Diane Carroll), its incomprehensible Wookiee dialogue, the Boba Fett cartoon, the Jefferson Starship segment, its ratings, Lucas's later disavowals, and its availability. The episode closes with listener mail about the Voynich Manuscript and a sign-off.
topics: Jefferson Starship Light the Sky on Fire

segments.title: Opening banter and Life Day
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter about Star Wars Day and the upcoming Star Wars film, then introduce Life Day, the Wookiee holiday that inspired the 1978 special, and promise a rundown of the special's notoriety.

segments.title: Origins: Lucas, CBS, and the Wookiee Bible
segments.summary: The hosts explain how CBS approached George Lucas after Star Wars became a hit, how Lucas proposed a Wookiee-centered story set on Kazook, and how his forty-page Wookiee Bible shaped the idea.

segments.title: Variety show concept and creative team
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why the special became a variety show, the decline of the genre by 1978, and the writers and director hired, including Bruce Vilanch, Lenny Ripps, the Welch family, and David Acomba, who left early.

segments.title: Cast and reluctant performers
segments.summary: The hosts cover the cast's limited leverage, Harrison Ford's visible reluctance, Mark Hamill's refusal to sing, and the involvement of Harvey Korman and Bea Arthur.

segments.title: Plot and incomprehensible Wookiee dialogue
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck outline the plot of Chewbacca trying to reach Kazook for Life Day, and describe the roughly ten minutes of subtitle-free Wookiee dialogue and the family's nicknames, including Itchy, Lumpy, and Malla.

segments.title: Cantina, Art Carney, and the softcore hologram
segments.summary: The hosts describe Art Carney's trader character, the Mos Eisley cantina sequence with Bea Arthur, Diane Carroll's segment with the hair dryer virtual-reality tape, and the gross tone of the special.

segments.title: Jefferson Starship, Boba Fett cartoon, and the ending
segments.summary: The hosts recount the Jefferson Starship music video played on the hologram, the Boba Fett cartoon watched by Lumpy that introduced the character, and the ending in which a stormtrooper trips and falls to his death and Carrie Fisher sings the Life Day song.

segments.title: Production history, ratings, and Lucas's disavowal
segments.summary: The hosts cover the original director's departure, Steve Binder's completion of the special, its 1978 broadcast and ratings, Lucas's later downplaying of it, and the video release and DVD extras that never happened.

segments.title: Viewing options, commentary, and final thoughts
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Mystery Science Theater 3000 riff track, the availability of copies online, the lack of a laugh track, and their final opinions of the special.

segments.title: Listener mail on the Voynich Manuscript
segments.summary: A listener writes about the Voynich Manuscript podcast, commenting on theories about its language, and shares how the show fits into their commute and noise-blocking routine.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and give contact and website information.
